questions.question: 79112. Which of the following is NOT one of the three cardinal biochemical features of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
questions.explain:
The cardinal biochemical triad of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) consists of:
​Hyperglycaemia
​Hyperketonaemia
​Metabolic acidosis Severe hyperosmolality without significant ketoacidosis is characteristic of HHS, not DKA.

questions.question: 79111. Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) belongs to which of the following virus families?
questions.explain: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) is an enveloped, single-stranded RNA virus that belongs to the Flavivirus family (genus Hepacivirus).

questions.question: 79110. Which of the following physical signs is a cardinal feature of Acute Left Ventricular Failure (ALVF)?
questions.explain:
Cardinal signs of Left Ventricular Failure (LVF) arise from pulmonary venous congestion and reduced left cardiac output.
These include Pulsus alternans (alternating strong and weak arterial pulses), Tachycardia, Gallop rhythm (S_3), and Bilateral basal crepitations in the lungs. Raised JVP, tender hepatomegaly, and dependent edema are features of Right Heart Failure.

questions.question: 79109. What pattern of fever is characteristic of dengue infection, typically featuring a break on day 4 or 5 followed by recrudescence?
questions.explain: Dengue fever often exhibits a biphasic or saddle-back temperature curve—where high fever drops on the 4th or 5th day, only to spike again (recrudescence) before resolving completely around days 7–8.

questions.question: 79108. Why are hand instruments preferred over rotary tools during the initial finishing of Glass Ionomer Cement restorations?
questions.option1: To speed up the chemical setting reaction
questions.option2: To prevent ditching at the restoration margins
questions.option3: To increase the rate of fluoride release
questions.option4: To convert conventional GIC into resin-modified GIC
questions.explain:
Under Finishing, excess material is trimmed from margins. Hand instruments are preferred over rotary tools specifically to avoid ditching the relatively immature cement surface.

​Final, thorough finishing with rotary tools, if required, is delayed until after 24 hours to allow complete maturation of the polysalt matrix.

questions.question: 79107. The quality of light passing through an object in a diffuse manner, revealing only a distorted image, is termed:
questions.explain:
Opacity: Light cannot pass through; no image seen.

​Translucency: Light passes through in a diffuse manner; distorted image seen.

​Transparency: Light passes through clearly; undistorted image seen.

questions.question: 79106. Which force of attraction occurs between molecules or atoms of the same species?
questions.explain: Cohesion is the force of molecular attraction between molecules or atoms of the same species. Adhesion occurs between molecules of two different species.

questions.question: 79105. What key physical requirement must an ideal inlay casting wax meet during the burnout process at 500 °C?
questions.option1: It must expand by at least 5% to compensate for metal shrinkage
questions.option2: It must vaporize completely without leaving any residue
questions.option3: It must harden into an insoluble ceramic framework
questions.option4: It must absorb water and exhibit imbibition
questions.explain: During burnout at 500 °C, the wax must vaporize completely without leaving any ash or solid residue that could contaminate the mold cavity during metal casting.

questions.question: 79104. What component constitutes the largest weight percentage (60%) in Alginate impression material?
questions.explain: Diatomaceous earth (60% wt.): Acts as the primary filler to give the powder bulk and control the flexibility and strength of the set gel.

questions.question: 79103. A deep bite present during the early stages of primary dentition is naturally reduced by which of the following factors?
questions.option3: Forward movement of the mandible due to growth
questions.explain:
Early primary dentition often exhibits a deep bite because primary incisors are relatively upright.
This deep bite is naturally corrected as developmental growth proceeds due to three main mechanisms:​
Eruption of primary molars (establishing vertical dimension).

​Physiological attrition/wear of the incisal edges.

​Forward growth and movement of the mandible.

questions.question: 79102. Which orthodontic intervention is specifically indicated for children aged 5 to 8 years?
questions.explain:
​Under 5 years: Arch repositioning in cleft lip/palate.

​5–8 years: Space maintenance, guided eruption, disking, habits management, and interceptive Class III/orthopedic appliances.

​8–12 years: Serial extractions, extraction of poor first permanent molars, and comprehensive fixed/removable appliances.

questions.question: 79101. What developmental phenomenon occurs around 8 to 9 years of age when developing upper permanent canines cause temporary distal divergence of upper central incisors?
questions.explain:
Broadbent's phenomenon (or Ugly Duckling Stage) is a self-correcting transient phase during mixed dentition.
As upper permanent canines erupt, they press against the roots of lateral and central incisors, causing mesial displacement of the roots and distal tilting/divergence of the crowns, creating a temporary midline space. This naturally resolves as the canines fully erupt into position.

questions.question: 79100. An Activator (Monoblock) functional appliance is CONTRAINDICATED in which of the following conditions?
questions.option1: Class II division 1 malocclusion in a growing child
questions.option2: Class II case with decreased lower facial height
questions.option3: Adult patient with completed active skeletal growth
questions.option4: Mild Class III malocclusion (using reverse activator)
questions.explain: Functional myofunctional appliances like the Activator rely on harnessing muscle force and active skeletal growth (growth spurt) to remodel the jaws and alveolar structures. Therefore, completed growth in adult patients is a primary contraindication. Other contraindications include severe crowding, high vertical growth angles, anterior open bite, and uncooperative patients.

questions.question: 79099. Which of the following orthodontic appliances is classified as a passive removable appliance?
questions.explain:
Passive appliances: Remain passive in the oral cavity without exerting active force (e.g., space maintainers, retention appliances, tongue guards).

​Functional appliances: Modify muscle forces to affect teeth and bone (e.g., Oral Screen, Andresen appliance, Frankel's Functional Regulator, Bimolar appliance).

​Mechanical appliances: Utilize springs, elastics, or screws to exert active forces.

questions.question: 79098. Extra-oral anchorage derived from the back of the neck is classified as:
questions.explain: Extra-oral anchorage utilizes anatomical regions outside the oral cavity. Cervical pull headgears anchor against the posterior neck region (cervical spine region) to deliver force. In contrast, high-pull headgears utilize the occipital or parietal regions, while face masks/reverse pull headgears utilize forehead and chin support.

questions.question: 79097. Which structural components are ABSENT in viruses?
questions.explain: Viruses are acellular obligate intracellular entities. They lack metabolic machinery, having no cytoplasm, mitochondria, or ribosomes, and depend completely on host cell machinery for protein synthesis and replication.

questions.question: 79096. Which site in the brain is most commonly involved by metastatic tumors?
questions.explain: Metastatic brain tumors typically present as multiple, well-circumscribed nodules located at the gray-white matter junction, where blood flow slows down in small vessel branching points, favoring tumor cell arrest.

questions.question: 79095. Which mediator does NOT produce fever during an inflammatory response?
questions.explain:
Pyrogens (Fever producers): Prostaglandins, TNF (Tumor Necrosis Factor), and IL-1 (Interleukin-1) act on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center to induce fever.

​C5a: Functions primarily as a powerful chemotactic agent for neutrophils and an anaphylatoxin, rather than an endogenous pyrogen.

questions.question: 79094. what is the primary cause of transudate formation in conditions like congestive heart failure?
questions.option4: Secretion of inflammatory mediators like bradykinin
questions.explain: Transudate formation in conditions like congestive heart failure is driven by increased venous hydrostatic pressure pushing fluid out of vessels without increasing inter-endothelial gaps or vascular permeability.

questions.question: 79093. What is the correct physiological rationale for the cardinal sign Dolor  in acute inflammation?
questions.option2: Exudation of fluid leading to edema
questions.option3: Stretching of pain receptors by inflammatory exudates and chemical mediators
questions.option4: Fibroplasia and metaplasia of surrounding tissues
questions.explain:
Rubor (Redness) & Calor (Heat): Caused by vascular dilation and increased blood flow.

​Tumor (Swelling): Caused by exudation of fluid and edema.

​Dolor (Pain): Caused by stretching of pain receptors from fluid accumulation (exudate) along with chemical mediators like bradykinin.

questions.question: 79092. Which of the following is NOT listed as an adverse effect of using mouthwash?
questions.option2: Dry mouth due to stenosis of the salivary duct
questions.explain:
Adverse Effects of Mouthwash:​
1.Staining of the tooth
​2.Taste disturbance (dysgeusia) due to blocking of the taste buds
​3.Dry mouth due to stenosis of the salivary duct
​4.Burning sensation of the oral cavity due to irritation of nerve endings
​5.May cause canker sores

questions.question: 79091. Which of the following water filtration methods removes fluoride from drinking water?
questions.explain:
Water Filters that Remove Fluoride: Reverse osmosis, bone charcoal filters, distillation, or ion exchange methods remove fluoride from water.

​Water Filters that Retain Fluoride: Normal membrane filters, ceramic filters, and carbon filters retain fluoride in the filtered water.

questions.question: 79090. Carbamazepine is indicated for which of the following conditions?
questions.explain:
Indications of Carbamazepine:​
Epilepsy: Partial seizures (All types: Simple & complex) and Tonic-clonic generalized seizures.

​Trigeminal neuralgia.

​Mania: Bipolar depression (used as a mood stabilizer).

questions.question: 79089. ​A patient is prescribed Rivaroxaban. What is the mode of action of this oral anticoagulant?
questions.explain:
Direct Factor Xa Inhibitors (Oral): Include Rivaroxaban, Apixaban, and Edoxaban.

​Direct Thrombin Inhibitors (Oral): Include Dabigatran.

​Vitamin K Antagonists (Oral): Include Warfarin and Coumarins.

questions.question: 79088. Which route of drug elimination is primary for volatile anesthetics such as Halothane and Nitrous Oxide?
questions.explain:
Pulmonary Elimination: Volatile substances and gases are excreted primarily through the lungs (exhalation).
Examples include volatile anesthetics, Ethanol, Halothane, Alcohol, and Nitrous Oxide.

​Renal Route: Responsible for almost all drugs except those strongly bound to plasma proteins.

​Hepatic Route: Involves drug metabolism/biliary excretion (e.g., Digoxin, Morphine, Propranolol, Rifampicin).

questions.question: 79087. Which of the following antimicrobial agents is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to the risk of causing neonatal 'grey baby' syndrome?
questions.explain:
Chloramphenicol is contraindicated in pregnancy because it can cross the placenta and lead to neonatal 'grey baby' syndrome, characterized by circulatory collapse, hypotension, and cyanosis in newborns.

​Tetracyclines cause fetal dental discoloration and skeletal abnormalities.

​Trimethoprim is teratogenic primarily in the first trimester.

​Fluconazole is teratogenic at high doses.

questions.question: 79086. Which of the following conditions is an example of Hypotonic (Hyponatremic) Dehydration?
questions.explain:
​Hypotonic Dehydration: Occurs in conditions where sodium loss exceeds water loss, such as diuretic use, Addison's disease (adrenal insufficiency), and renal salt-wasting.

​Diabetes insipidus and fever cause hypertonic dehydration (pure or predominant water loss).

​Hemorrhage, diarrhea, and vomiting typically cause isotonic dehydration.

questions.question: 79085. What clinical term defines the complete absence of the sense of taste?
questions.explain:
Ageusia: Complete absence of the sense of taste.
​Hypogeusia: Diminished taste sensitivity.
​Dysgeusia: Disturbed or perverted sense of taste.

questions.question: 79084. Which Brodmann area is classified as the primary motor area (located in the frontal lobe) responsible for controlling contralateral motor activity?
questions.explain:
Brodmann Area 4 (Frontal lobe): Represents the primary motor area, which directly controls voluntary contralateral motor activity.

​Brodmann Area 6: Represents the premotor area / secondary motor area, which programs and assists the activity of the primary motor area.

​Brodmann Areas 3, 1, 2: Represent the primary somesthetic area in the parietal lobe.

​Brodmann Areas 44, 45: Form Broca's motor speech area in the frontal lobe.

questions.question: 79083. Which of the following conditions is a primary cause of Anemic Hypoxia?
questions.explain:
Anemic Hypoxia occurs when there is a reduction in available functional hemoglobin, decreasing the total O2 carrying capacity of blood while arterial PO2 remains normal.

​Major causes include anemia, carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning (due to carboxyhemoglobin formation), and methemoglobinemia.

​High altitude causes hypoxic hypoxia; congestive heart failure causes stagnant hypoxia; cyanide poisoning causes histotoxic hypoxia.

questions.question: 79082. ​What classic shape does the Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve exhibit?
questions.explain:
The oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve represents the relationship between the partial pressure of oxygen (\text{PO}_2) and percent saturation of hemoglobin.

​The curve is characteristically sigmoid-shaped (S-shaped) due to cooperative binding of oxygen to the four subunits of the hemoglobin molecule.

questions.question: 79081. Which of the following volatile substances is EXCRETED by the lungs?
questions.explain:
Excretory Function of Lungs:
The lungs excrete several volatile substances and metabolic byproducts in exhaled breath, including ammonia, ketone bodies (e.g., acetone in diabetic ketoacidosis), essential oils, alcohol, and water vapor.

questions.question: 79080. Which of the following conditions is associated with a DECREASED Cardiac Output (CO)?
questions.explain:
Pathological causes of Decreased Cardiac Output:
Include Hypothyroidism, hemorrhage, congestive cardiac failure, shock, atrial fibrillation, and incomplete heart block.

​Pathological causes of Increased Cardiac Output:
Include Hyperthyroidism, Anemia, Fever, Hypoxia, Fibrillation & Flutter, Paget’s disease, and Arteriovenous fistula.

questions.question: 79079. which of the following is classified as an Observational Analytical (Explanatory) study?
questions.explain:
Observational Descriptive Studies: Case study, case series, cross-sectional study, community survey, ecological study (studies without a comparison group).

​Observational Analytical Studies: Case-control study, cohort study, and cross-sectional study (studies with a comparison group).

​Experimental Studies: Clinical trials, Randomized Controlled Trials (RCT), quasi-experimental studies, and community field trials (studies involving active intervention).

questions.question: 79078. Which type of consent is implied through a patient's voluntary actions, such as rolling up a sleeve for a blood sample draw?
questions.explain:
Implied Consent: Inferred non-verbally through the patient's actions or behavior (e.g., holding out an arm or rolling up a sleeve).

​Verbal/Expressed Consent: Explicitly stated verbally for minor or routine procedures.

​Written Consent: Documented via a signed consent form, required for invasive or high-risk surgical procedures.

​Therapeutic Privilege: A rare ethical exception where full disclosure may be withheld if it would cause severe, foreseeable harm to the patient.

questions.question: 79077. which form of defamation is conveyed in a permanent form?
questions.explain:
Libel: Refers to defamatory statements expressed in a permanent form, such as written text, print, carving, cartoons, films, or broadcasts on radio or television.

​Slander: Refers to defamation presented in a transitory (non-permanent) form, such as spoken words or gestures.

​Assault: Defined as an act by which a person causes another to immediately anticipate unlawful contact with their person.

questions.question: 79076. Which of the following age-related changes occurs in dental enamel over time?
questions.option1: Water content increases while crystal size decreases
questions.option2: Permeability increases due to widening of enamel pores
questions.option3: Enamel becomes less permeable due to increased absorption of ions and increased crystal size
questions.option4: Incidence of dental caries increases significantly in older adults
questions.explain:
Permeability Changes: As enamel ages, it behaves as a semipermeable membrane, and its permeability decreases due to increased ion absorption and increased crystal size.

​Water Content: Water content in enamel decreases with age.

​Caries Susceptibility: There is a decreased incidence of caries and an increased resistance to caries with advancing age.

​Surface Features: Perikymata disappear from the enamel surface over time, with localized increases in Na+ and F- ions.

questions.question: 79075. Which of the following dental/oral features is characteristic of Down’s syndrome?
questions.option2: Class III malocclusion with hypoplastic maxilla and low caries activity
questions.explain:
Down’s syndrome oral manifestations include a hypoplastic maxilla leading to Class III malocclusion, a protrusive, fissured, and hypotonic tongue (macroglossia), lip hypotonia, and open bite.

​Notably, patients with Down’s syndrome typically show low caries activity, despite having gross plaque accumulation and rapidly progressive periodontal disease.

​Other dental findings include oligodontia (missing teeth), delayed eruption of permanent teeth, hypoplastic dental defects, short roots, and bruxism.

questions.question: 79074. Which chromosome type has its centromere located at the very end and is not normally seen in humans?
questions.explain:
​Telocentric Chromosomes: The centromere is positioned at the extreme end of the chromosome, giving it an I-shape.
This type is not found in humans.

​Metacentric: The centromere is in the middle, forming a V-shape.

​Submetacentric: The centromere is slightly off-center, forming an L-shape.

​Acrocentric: The centromere is located near one end, forming a rod-shape.

questions.question: 79073. Which of the following cellular organelles is classified as a NON-MEMBRANOUS organelle?
questions.explain:
Non-membranous organelles lack a phospholipid membrane enclosure.
Key examples include Ribosomes and Centrioles/Centrosomes.

​Membranous organelles are surrounded by single or double lipid bilayer membranes.
Examples include:​
Mitochondria (double membrane)
​Endoplasmic Reticulum (Rough & Smooth)
​Golgi Complex
​Lysosomes
​Peroxisomes

questions.question: 79072. Tissue macrophages are derived from which circulating blood cell lineage?
questions.explain: ​Monocytes circulate in the bloodstream and migrate into tissues, where they differentiate into tissue-specific macrophages (e.g., Kupffer cells in the liver, alveolar macrophages in the lungs, osteoclasts in bone, and histiocytes in connective tissue).

questions.question: 79071. ​Which of the following lymphoid organs possesses both afferent and efferent lymph vessels?
questions.explain:
Lymph Node:
It is unique among the primary and secondary lymphoid organs because it acts as a filter for lymph. Therefore, it possesses both afferent lymph vessels (which bring lymph into the node) and efferent lymph vessels (which carry lymph away).

​Spleen & Thymus:
Both the spleen and the thymus contain only efferent lymph vessels (no afferent lymphatics entering them). The spleen filters blood rather than lymph.

questions.question: 79070. Largest cell in the human body is_____?
questions.explain:
The ovum (egg cell) is the largest cell in the human body by diameter, measuring about 100–120 µm.

Other options:

*Osteocyte → mature bone cell; much smaller.

*Glial cell → supporting cell of the nervous system.

*Myelin cells → not considered the largest cell.

questions.question: 79069. Bell's palsy affects which nerve?
questions.explain: Bell's palsy is a condition that causes temporary paralysis or weakness of the muscles in the face. It is caused by damage to the facial nerve (the 7th cranial nerve). The facial nerve controls the muscles of the face, so when it is damaged, the muscles on one side of the face can become weak or paralyzed.

questions.question: 79068. Which is not STD?
questions.explain:
Hepatitis A is not considered a sexually transmitted disease (STD). It is primarily transmitted through ingestion of contaminated food or water, or through close contact with an infected person.

It affects the liver but is not typically transmitted through sexual contact.

questions.question: 79067. Which of the following is NOT a cause/risk factor for cardiac arrest?
questions.explain:
Hyperglycemia itself is not a classic direct reversible cause of cardiac arrest.

Severe uncontrolled diabetes can contribute indirectly to cardiovascular disease, but it is not one of the standard immediate causes.

The other options are cause/risk factor for cardiac arrest.

questions.question: 79066. Primary function of the skin is ____?
questions.explain:
The primary function of the skin is to act as a protective barrier between the body and the external environment.

It protects the body from:

Microorganisms and infection,
Excessive water loss,
UV radiation,
Physical and chemical injury.

questions.question: 79065. Which one is the leading cause of death in burn victims?
questions.explain:
Sepsis and its complications are a major cause of death in patients with severe burns, particularly during the later course of burn injury.

Burns destroy the skin's protective barrier and cause immune dysfunction, making the patient highly susceptible to infection.

Bacteria can invade the wound → systemic infection → sepsis → septic shock → multi-organ failure.

questions.question: 79064. Burn injury to which of the following areas is considered to be the largest area according to the Rule of Nines?
questions.explain:
The Rule of Nines is used to estimate the total body surface area (TBSA) affected by burns in adults.

According to the adult Rule of Nines:
One entire leg -18% 
One entire arm-9%
Anterior trunk-18%
Head & neck-9%

Therefore, among the given options, one right leg = 18%, which is the largest single area listed.

questions.question: 79063. In an infant, the most preferred site for intramuscular (IM) injection is ______?
questions.explain: The vastus lateralis muscle (anterolateral thigh) is the preferred IM injection site for infants, because it is well developed and provides a relatively large, accessible muscle mass.
